programs.name: Tone I: String 1
programs.description: Circuit interpretation of String 1; the named row carries the body and the other rank supports the same instrument. An authored study, not a measured preset-board capture. A modeled bowed body enters before a lighter moving upper section. Different harmonic weights and restrained chorus give the ranks depth; pressure adds bow intensity and gentle vibrato. A gently brighter body with a clean, controlled key release.

programs.name: Tone II: String 2
programs.description: Circuit interpretation of String 2; the named row carries the body and the other rank supports the same instrument. An authored study, not a measured preset-board capture. Two closely tuned modeled bow sections speak at slightly different times without chorus. Distinct harmonic weights and restrained motion suggest a small group while preserving clear note changes. A warmer filter balance and a slightly longer body decay.

programs.name: Tone I: String 3
programs.description: Circuit interpretation of String 3; the named row carries the body and the other rank supports the same instrument. An authored study, not a measured preset-board capture. A soft bowed harmonic body rises over 0.85 seconds and the brighter section follows over 1.15 seconds. Hold the chord through the opening to hear their separate spectral blooms and long overlapping releases. A gently brighter body with a clean, controlled key release.

programs.name: Tone II: String 4
programs.description: Circuit interpretation of String 4; the named row carries the body and the other rank supports the same instrument. An authored study, not a measured preset-board capture. Two pulse sections evolve at distinct slow rates, with the second filter bloom arriving later. Reduced PWM excursion and chorus preserve a steady pitch center while the harmonic balance keeps moving. A warmer filter balance and a slightly longer body decay.

programs.name: Tone I: Brass 1
programs.description: Circuit interpretation of Brass 1; the named row carries the body and the other rank supports the same instrument. An authored study, not a measured preset-board capture. A rounded harmonic body enters before the brighter circuit rank completes its swell. The lip-like attack settles into a stable center; pressure opens the held chord and the wheel adds restrained vibrato. A gently brighter body with a clean, controlled key release.

programs.name: Tone II: Brass 2
programs.description: Circuit interpretation of Brass 2; the named row carries the body and the other rank supports the same instrument. An authored study, not a measured preset-board capture. A modeled 16' brass foundation supports an 8' circuit crown. Staggered filter rises broaden the swell while the darker lower spectrum preserves weight; pressure brings forward the upper rank. A warmer filter balance and a slightly longer body decay.

programs.name: Tone I: Flute
programs.description: Circuit interpretation of Flute; the named row carries the body and the other rank supports the same instrument. An authored study, not a measured preset-board capture. A modeled flute harmonic body carries a separately sustained, quiet air stream. Velocity changes the tongued onset and upper-partial balance; pressure adds breath intensity and restrained vibrato without turning the line into a sine whistle. A gently brighter body with a clean, controlled key release.

programs.name: Tone II: Brass 3
programs.description: Circuit interpretation of Brass 3; the named row carries the body and the other rank supports the same instrument. An authored study, not a measured preset-board capture. Two closely tuned harmonic brass ranks form a warm horn section. Their soft, staggered attacks and differently weighted upper harmonics give depth without a heavy chorus; pressure brings out the brass bloom. A warmer filter balance and a slightly longer body decay.

programs.name: Tone I: E. Piano
programs.description: Circuit interpretation of E. Piano; the named row carries the body and the other rank supports the same instrument. An authored study, not a measured preset-board capture. A warm tine body with individually fading overtones and a velocity-sensitive upper bark. The short strike falls away into a rounded ringing fundamental; key release damps the note. A gently brighter body with a clean, controlled key release.

programs.name: Tone II: Bass
programs.description: Circuit interpretation of Bass; the named row carries the body and the other rank supports the same instrument. An authored study, not a measured preset-board capture. A firm 16-foot saw-and-sine body carries a brisk, separately decaying 8-foot pulse edge. A cleaner low sustain and more gradual filter settling give repeated notes weight without leaving an abrasive upper buzz. A warmer filter balance and a slightly longer body decay.

programs.name: Tone I: Clavichord 1
programs.description: Circuit interpretation of Clavichord 1; the named row carries the body and the other rank supports the same instrument. An authored study, not a measured preset-board capture. A dry tangent-excited string spectrum with a short upper snap. Its high partials damp independently, leaving a small clear body; velocity changes the edge as well as the level. A gently brighter body with a clean, controlled key release.

programs.name: Tone II: Clavichord 2
programs.description: Circuit interpretation of Clavichord 2; the named row carries the body and the other rank supports the same instrument. An authored study, not a measured preset-board capture. A darker tangent string with a shorter, nasal decay. A restrained resonant pulse remains in the attack, while independent upper-partial damping keeps the held tail from becoming an electronic buzz. A warmer filter balance and a slightly longer body decay.

programs.name: Tone I: Harpsichord 1
programs.description: Circuit interpretation of Harpsichord 1; the named row carries the body and the other rank supports the same instrument. An authored study, not a measured preset-board capture. A bright quill-plucked string has a notched harmonic spectrum and individually fading upper partials. The short second rank marks the quill release; nearly even strike dynamics and prompt key damping keep the register articulate. A gently brighter body with a clean, controlled key release.

programs.name: Tone II: Harpsichord 2
programs.description: Circuit interpretation of Harpsichord 2; the named row carries the body and the other rank supports the same instrument. An authored study, not a measured preset-board capture. Coupled quill-plucked 8-foot and 4-foot strings with independent harmonic losses. The octave course speaks brightly then recedes, while the lower course rings; the two registers keep nearly even strike dynamics. A warmer filter balance and a slightly longer body decay.

programs.name: Tone I: Organ 1
programs.description: Circuit interpretation of Organ 1; the named row carries the body and the other rank supports the same instrument. An authored study, not a measured preset-board capture. An 8' flute-like harmonic registration is supported by a lighter 4' stop. Soft fast gates, straight tuning and velocity-independent sustain keep chord voicings clear, with more body than two pure sines. A gently brighter body with a clean, controlled key release.

programs.name: Tone II: Organ 2
programs.description: Circuit interpretation of Organ 2; the named row carries the body and the other rank supports the same instrument. An authored study, not a measured preset-board capture. A steady harmonic registration and pulse edge form a reed-organ color. Distinct bellows-like onsets soften the two 8' ranks, while velocity-independent keying and restrained tuning keep held chords stable. A warmer filter balance and a slightly longer body decay.

programs.name: Tone I: Guitar 1
programs.description: Circuit interpretation of Guitar 1; the named row carries the body and the other rank supports the same instrument. An authored study, not a measured preset-board capture. A nylon-like plucked-string spectrum has a warm body and a brief finger/pick edge. The excitation notch and faster high-partial losses let the clear lower string outlast the attack; harder playing brightens the strike. A gently brighter body with a clean, controlled key release.

programs.name: Tone II: Guitar 2
programs.description: Circuit interpretation of Guitar 2; the named row carries the body and the other rank supports the same instrument. An authored study, not a measured preset-board capture. A brighter steel-string body carries a firmer pick and longer upper shimmer than Guitar I. Independently damping partials soften the attack naturally above the ringing lower string. A warmer filter balance and a slightly longer body decay.

programs.name: Tone I: Funky 1
programs.description: Circuit interpretation of Funky 1; the named row carries the body and the other rank supports the same instrument. An authored study, not a measured preset-board capture. A compact tangent-string snap joins a fast resonant filter attack. Independent upper losses clarify repeated notes while the circuit pulse retains the dry, rhythmic wah character. A gently brighter body with a clean, controlled key release.

programs.name: Tone II: Funky 2
programs.description: Circuit interpretation of Funky 2; the named row carries the body and the other rank supports the same instrument. An authored study, not a measured preset-board capture. A more open plucked-string body sits inside the slower wah-shaped circuit contour. The brief upper snap marks the strike, then independently damping string partials leave a rounded, expressive tail. A warmer filter balance and a slightly longer body decay.

programs.name: Tone I: Funky 3
programs.description: Circuit interpretation of Funky 3; the named row carries the body and the other rank supports the same instrument. An authored study, not a measured preset-board capture. A tangent-string snap and compact resonant wah share the attack. The dry string body adds definition between the filter accents; hard playing brings out the upper rank without leaving a held pad. A gently brighter body with a clean, controlled key release.

programs.name: Tone II: Funky 4
programs.description: Circuit interpretation of Funky 4; the named row carries the body and the other rank supports the same instrument. An authored study, not a measured preset-board capture. A compact tangent-string snap joins a fast resonant filter attack. Independent upper losses clarify repeated notes while the circuit pulse retains the dry, rhythmic wah character. A warmer filter balance and a slightly longer body decay.

programs.name: Replicant Brass
programs.description: A dark circuit body opens slowly beneath a later luminous upper rank. Reduced chorus and a steadier pitch center leave the evolving filter bloom clear; pressure adds intensity and gentle vibrato. A gently brighter body with a clean, controlled key release.

programs.name: Runner Brass
programs.description: A soft harmonic core takes over a second to rise while a later circuit rank completes the bright bloom. The upper section remains lighter during the long overlap, giving sustained chords depth and a clear center. A slower opening gesture and a longer decay and release.

programs.name: French Horn
programs.description: A dark, stable horn body with a restrained upper lip edge and rounded breath release. Pressure favors expressive level over brightness; the harmonic body remains clear through middle and lower-register phrasing. A warmer filter balance and a slightly longer body decay.

programs.name: Breathing Brass
programs.description: A slow, shallow ring component shades a warm harmonic-supported chord. The lighter circuit rank opens later, and the ring motion emerges gently so held chords breathe without a hard amplitude pulse. A covered upper register and a gently rounded release.

programs.name: Cinema Strings
programs.description: A modeled bowed body enters before a lighter moving upper section. Different harmonic weights and restrained chorus give the ranks depth; pressure adds bow intensity and gentle vibrato. The two circuit ranks spread gently across stereo, retaining stable pitch.

programs.name: Glass Strings
programs.description: An 8' harmonic bowed body supports a delicate 2' circuit glint. The upper register opens later and stays light, adding a glassy edge without overtaking the string center. A more open harmonic spectrum with a slightly tighter decay.

programs.name: Distant Oceans
programs.description: A dark modeled bowed body supports covered pulse overtones. Slow harmonic openings and a restrained chorus keep the low center intact while the long releases join soft, sombre chords. Restrained high harmonics with a longer, softer ending. A high-pass contour keeps the distant texture light beneath a melody.

programs.name: Dry Ensemble
programs.description: Dry dual-rank strings with restrained detuning, a clear bow onset and pressure-controlled brightness. No chorus.

programs.name: 1982 Pad
programs.description: A dark saw foundation supports a later pulse glow, a broad stereo field, chorus and a faint slow ring beat. Long, unequal releases leave a warm cinematic tail after the upper color recedes. A warmer filter balance and a slightly longer body decay. A very slow ring-modulator movement shades the sustained chord.

programs.name: Sweep VCA
programs.description: A warm body and brighter pulse rank share gentle 3.8 Hz SUB amplitude motion. The circuit tremolo adds stereo movement while the whole chord rises and falls smoothly without chopping to silence. A slower opening gesture and a longer decay and release.

programs.name: Blade Choir
programs.description: A covered 16' vowel-like body sits beneath a quiet 8' nasal band. Unequal rank attacks give this low choir color depth without a large detuned wobble. A covered upper register and a gently rounded release.

programs.name: Dry Bass
programs.description: A firm 16-foot saw-and-sine body carries a brisk, separately decaying 8-foot pulse edge. A cleaner low sustain and more gradual filter settling give repeated notes weight without leaving an abrasive upper buzz. A gently brighter body with a clean, controlled key release.

programs.name: Resonant Bass
programs.description: A fast resonant upper sweep settles above a firm sine-supported low note. The body opens more slowly than the edge, keeping the attack lively while the low sustain remains focused. A quicker, brighter edge with a deliberately short attack body.

programs.name: Bass Stack
programs.description: Two 8-foot ranks reinforce the same bass register, with a bright opening and a compact lower body. Play in the low register.

programs.name: Ribbon Lead
programs.description: A smooth, centered lead for ribbon gestures. Short portamento and a small upward onset scoop connect phrases; a restrained upper edge keeps large slides readable. A gently brighter body with a clean, controlled key release.

programs.name: Metal Lead
programs.description: A clean center tone mixed with 280 Hz ring sidebands for a metallic edge. The restrained wet blend preserves pitch identity while pressure brightens the source. A forward upper edge with a compact attack and decay.

programs.name: Analog Piano
programs.description: A firm hammer excites a full struck-string spectrum with slight stiffness and controlled unison beating. The bright partials fall away at different rates above a long rounded body; key release damps the strings promptly. A gently brighter body with a clean, controlled key release.

programs.name: Bright Keys
programs.description: A bright tine attack resolves into a smooth electric body with independently softening overtones. Shallow chorus motion shades the long decay while the dry strike keeps chord changes clear. A more open harmonic spectrum with a slightly tighter decay.

programs.name: Ring Bell
programs.description: A rounded wooden-mode body supports a short metallic upper mallet, then feeds the ring circuit. Hard strikes expose the upper clang; its rapid losses leave a softer resonating body behind. A gently brighter body with a clean, controlled key release.

programs.name: Laser Sweep
programs.description: A low body and later upper pulse bloom as the ring carrier rises, then falls over several seconds. Different filter and amplitude swells make the motion unfold in layers. A quicker, brighter edge with a deliberately short attack body.

programs.name: Arp Motion
programs.description: Hold two to four notes around C3-C4 for eight notes per second across two octaves. A short octave accent and one-second filter cycle articulate the ascent. A covered upper register and a gently rounded release.

programs.name: Init Patch
programs.description: A clean starting point on the circuit engine: one saw rank, open filter, no modulation. A gently brighter body with a clean, controlled key release.

programs.name: Amber Brass 1
programs.description: A soft harmonic center supports a dark circuit halo that enters later. Shallow pulse movement and restrained chorus keep the long release smooth; pressure adds warmth and level without a sharp edge. A warmer filter balance and a slightly longer body decay.

programs.name: Velvet Brass 2
programs.description: A dark, stable horn body with a restrained upper lip edge and rounded breath release. Pressure favors expressive level over brightness; the harmonic body remains clear through middle and lower-register phrasing. A covered upper register and a gently rounded release.

programs.name: Distant Brass 3
programs.description: A dark harmonic center supports a softened, later circuit section. Slower entrances and a long diffuse release suggest distance, while reduced chorus preserves chord pitch and the upper edge stays subdued. Restrained high harmonics with a longer, softer ending.

programs.name: Neon Brass 4
programs.description: An assertive 8' harmonic section carries a shorter 4' circuit crown. Velocity sharpens the lip-like onset, and the lighter octave settles quickly so the played root stays strong through the held chord. A forward upper edge with a compact attack and decay.

programs.name: Hollow Brass 5
programs.description: A compact, bright harmonic brass body meets a narrow nasal circuit edge. A quick tongue-like accent settles before the held note; pressure sharpens the focus and adds a small expressive vibrato. A lightly emphasized filter resonance over a longer body.

programs.name: Golden Brass 6
programs.description: Two closely tuned harmonic brass ranks form a warm horn section. Their soft, staggered attacks and differently weighted upper harmonics give depth without a heavy chorus; pressure brings out the brass bloom. A gently brighter body with a clean, controlled key release.

programs.name: Frozen Brass 7
programs.description: A broad harmonic brass body and lighter circuit crown are balanced for wide keyboard voicings. A gentle brilliance contour and restrained treble level keep upper notes from becoming sharp while low chords retain their center. Steadier tuning and a longer ringing or held body.

programs.name: Electric Brass 8
programs.description: Soft strikes retain a rounded circuit body; hard strikes add a much shorter resonant upper bite. The accent drops away before the body, leaving pressure to shape the held bloom. A quicker, brighter edge with a deliberately short attack body.

programs.name: Midnight Brass 9
programs.description: Two 16' harmonic brass ranks combine a rounded low foundation with a smaller lip edge. A slower body attack and short breath-like release give weight to low phrases without continual pitch wobble. Darkened upper harmonics with a slightly longer body.

programs.name: Slow Brass 10
programs.description: A harmonic brass body rises for 1.6 seconds before the brighter upper section completes the crescendo. Hold the chord through the opening, then use pressure to increase harmonic intensity without retriggering the entrance. A slower opening gesture and a longer decay and release.

programs.name: Bright Brass 11
programs.description: Fast circuit brass comping with a rounded sustaining center and a brief, bright upper accent. Greater attack contrast and a tighter upper release keep rhythmic chord changes clear. A more open harmonic spectrum with a slightly tighter decay.

programs.name: Dark Brass 12
programs.description: A stable harmonic brass body combines with a narrow reed-colored upper rank. Their staggered attacks and different pressure response let the reed edge emerge expressively without replacing the brass foundation. A strongly covered harmonic spectrum with a tidy release.

programs.name: Wide Brass 13
programs.description: A weighty 16' harmonic foundation supports a later 8' brass section. Restrained chorus joins the differently voiced ranks while preserving the low center and their separate entrances. The two circuit ranks spread gently across stereo, retaining stable pitch.

programs.name: Soft Brass 14
programs.description: A dark, stable horn body with a restrained upper lip edge and rounded breath release. Pressure favors expressive level over brightness; the harmonic body remains clear through middle and lower-register phrasing. A restrained upper edge with a subtly cushioned onset.

programs.name: Amber Brass 15
programs.description: A rounded harmonic body enters before the brighter circuit rank completes its swell. The lip-like attack settles into a stable center; pressure opens the held chord and the wheel adds restrained vibrato. A warmer filter balance and a slightly longer body decay.

programs.name: Distant Brass 17
programs.description: A soft harmonic core takes over a second to rise while a later circuit rank completes the bright bloom. The upper section remains lighter during the long overlap, giving sustained chords depth and a clear center. Restrained high harmonics with a longer, softer ending.

programs.name: Neon Brass 18
programs.description: A bright brass attack relaxes rapidly into a quieter sustained harmonic body. The separate upper accent decays away, while velocity changes its spectral bite as well as its weight. A forward upper edge with a compact attack and decay.

programs.name: Hollow Brass 19
programs.description: A firm saw body precedes a moving saw-and-pulse horn edge. Slower, shallower pulse motion and a shorter upper bloom keep the synth identity rich while reducing the static, buzzy blend. A lightly emphasized filter resonance over a longer body.

programs.name: Golden Brass 20
programs.description: Straight-tuned 8' and 4' brass ranks combine harmonic depth with a lighter circuit edge. The upper octave speaks slightly later and settles lower, remaining present without competing with the root. A gently brighter body with a clean, controlled key release.

programs.name: Frozen Brass 21
programs.description: A warm harmonic-supported brass swell becomes darker after key release. The brighter circuit rank opens later and falls away sooner, producing a deliberate rise and closing gesture instead of a static pad tail. Steadier tuning and a longer ringing or held body.

programs.name: Electric Brass 22
programs.description: A compact, dry brass hit with a shaped harmonic attack beneath a shorter circuit bite. Both ranks die away on a held key; tight key releases keep repeated chords distinct. A quicker, brighter edge with a deliberately short attack body.

programs.name: Amber Strings 23
programs.description: Two closely tuned modeled bow sections speak at slightly different times without chorus. Distinct harmonic weights and restrained motion suggest a small group while preserving clear note changes. A warmer filter balance and a slightly longer body decay.

programs.name: Velvet Strings 24
programs.description: A soft modeled bowed body carries low pulse overtones with very shallow movement. Dark harmonic weighting and separately shaped long releases make a smooth, warm tail without a bright layer hovering above it. A covered upper register and a gently rounded release.

programs.name: Distant Strings 25
programs.description: A dark modeled bowed body supports covered pulse overtones. Slow harmonic openings and a restrained chorus keep the low center intact while the long releases join soft, sombre chords. Restrained high harmonics with a longer, softer ending.

programs.name: Neon Strings 26
programs.description: A firm upper bow burst decays into a quieter modeled harmonic body. Velocity shapes the bite and its weight; the independent accent disappears during the hold, leaving a clear sustained bow. A forward upper edge with a compact attack and decay.

programs.name: Hollow Strings 27
programs.description: A high-passed circuit section retains a narrow upper-string texture without losing every low harmonic. The thinner second rank enters later and relaxes sooner, making the distant sound airy rather than brittle. A lightly emphasized filter resonance over a longer body.

programs.name: Golden Strings 28
programs.description: A modeled bowed body enters before a lighter moving upper section. Different harmonic weights and restrained chorus give the ranks depth; pressure adds bow intensity and gentle vibrato. A gently brighter body with a clean, controlled key release.

programs.name: Frozen Strings 29

programs.name: Electric Strings 30
programs.description: Bright circuit saw sections use a fast ensemble chorus, steady sustain and very little touch dependence. A stronger lower foundation, quicker first rank and controlled detuning keep rhythmic chord changes immediate. A quicker, brighter edge with a deliberately short attack body.

programs.name: Midnight Strings 31
programs.description: A full 16' bowed harmonic body supports a shorter 8' bow edge. The darker low spectrum keeps weight beneath the articulation; pressure opens the upper harmonics without a broad ensemble wobble. Darkened upper harmonics with a slightly longer body.

programs.name: Slow Strings 32

programs.description: An 8' modeled bowed section carries a quieter 4' upper sheen. A quick bow onset, clear upper harmonics and restrained chorus preserve articulated lines, with pressure adding intensity after the attack. A more open harmonic spectrum with a slightly tighter decay.

programs.name: Dark Strings 34
programs.description: Modeled bow harmonics and a brighter circuit section share a keyboard contour. The low range stays soft while restrained treble brilliance and level keep wide voicings balanced across the keyboard. A strongly covered harmonic spectrum with a tidy release.

programs.name: Amber Strings 37
programs.description: A modeled bow body rises before the two harmonic ranges bloom over 1.1 and 1.5 seconds. Hold the chord to hear the brighter section emerge, then use pressure to increase bow intensity without losing the covered center. A warmer filter balance and a slightly longer body decay.

programs.name: Velvet Strings 38
programs.description: A quiet modeled bow bed gains harmonic weight and level under pressure. The lighter upper section enters later, and easing pressure returns the same held bow to a soft texture without retriggering. A covered upper register and a gently rounded release.

programs.name: Distant Strings 39
programs.description: A modeled bowed body holds beneath a separate filtered friction layer. The air opens quickly and fades to a restrained breath, while pressure supports the pitched body and the release stays clean. Restrained high harmonics with a longer, softer ending.

programs.name: Neon Strings 40
programs.description: Short modeled bow strokes return quickly to silence: a defined harmonic body follows an even shorter upper bite. Velocity changes the excitation as well as level; detached playing produces clean repeated strokes. A forward upper edge with a compact attack and decay.

programs.name: Hollow Strings 41
programs.description: Two pulse sections evolve at distinct slow rates, with the second filter bloom arriving later. Reduced PWM excursion and chorus preserve a steady pitch center while the harmonic balance keeps moving. A lightly emphasized filter resonance over a longer body.

programs.name: Golden Strings 42
programs.description: A strong 16' modeled bow body supports an 8' section with brighter, faster-speaking harmonics. Moderate chorus joins the sections while velocity gives articulated chords a clear opening weight. A gently brighter body with a clean, controlled key release.

programs.name: Frozen Strings 43
programs.description: A softly entering harmonic fifth joins an 8' modeled bowed body. The fifth has a lighter spectral weight and remains subordinate through the release; sparse voicings reveal the open interval clearly. Steadier tuning and a longer ringing or held body.

programs.name: Electric Strings 44
programs.description: Two circuit saw sections bloom at different rates before settling into a covered synth-string sustain. Restrained chorus, a steadier tuning center and separate long releases keep the texture lush without a smeared attack. A quicker, brighter edge with a deliberately short attack body.

programs.name: Midnight Strings 45
programs.description: A dry 16' modeled bowed body retains a warm fundamental beneath an independently fading low bow-friction onset. Pressure adds weight and restrained vibrato, with no octave layer or ensemble chorus. Darkened upper harmonics with a slightly longer body.

programs.name: Slow Strings 46
programs.description: An 8' harmonic bowed section is joined by a lighter, later 4' section. Different upper-partial weights and envelope timing keep both registers clear without hollowing the lower body. A slower opening gesture and a longer decay and release.

programs.name: Amber Pads 47
programs.description: A filtered saw with a small sine foundation and a quiet soft-pulse companion. Compact stereo motion and modest pressure brightness preserve the warm center. A warmer filter balance and a slightly longer body decay.

programs.name: Velvet Pads 48
programs.description: Softly filtered saw ranks overlap with shallow, unequal blooms. Modest detune and chorus make a dense, smooth chord; the second rank closes earlier on release. A covered upper register and a gently rounded release.

programs.name: Distant Pads 49
programs.description: A dark low-mid saw body appears before a dim pulse halo. Shallow filter movement, a quiet upper layer and long releases keep the sustained chord spacious and subdued. Restrained high harmonics with a longer, softer ending.

programs.name: Neon Pads 50
programs.description: A soft 8' chord supports a light 2' pulse shimmer. The high rank is deliberately opened for its register and enters late, separating the upper sparkle from the body. A forward upper edge with a compact attack and decay.

programs.name: Hollow Pads 51
programs.description: Near-square pulses emphasize a hollow odd-harmonic center. Shallow, slow width motion and differently filtered ranks soften the sound without making a thin nasal pulse. A lightly emphasized filter resonance over a longer body.

programs.name: Golden Pads 52
programs.description: Two softly entered pulse ranks suggest an open vowel. A low body band supports a brighter nasal band; this is a synthesized choir color. A gently brighter body with a clean, controlled key release.

programs.name: Frozen Pads 53
programs.description: A thin, bright 8' saw band supports a quiet 4' pulse sheen. Distinct high-pass bands and later upper entry create an icy texture; gently spread ranks supply stereo width under moderate chorus. Steadier tuning and a longer ringing or held body.

programs.name: Electric Pads 54
programs.description: Two pulse-only ranks use distinct PWM rates and depths. A steady low body anchors the moving upper harmonics, with modest chorus instead of excessive pitch detune. A quicker, brighter edge with a deliberately short attack body.

programs.name: Midnight Pads 55
programs.description: A covered 16' vowel-like body sits beneath a quiet 8' nasal band. Unequal rank attacks give this low choir color depth without a large detuned wobble. Darkened upper harmonics with a slightly longer body.

programs.name: Slow Pads 56
programs.description: A warm saw body fades in before a brighter moving pulse rank. Their filter blooms and release lengths overlap gently; pressure brings forward the upper color. A slower opening gesture and a longer decay and release.

programs.name: Bright Pads 57
programs.description: An 8' soft body supports a late 2' sine and pulse glint. The high rank has its own brighter filter and lower sustain, letting the glass color float above the chord. A more open harmonic spectrum with a slightly tighter decay.

programs.name: Dark Pads 58
programs.description: Stable 16' ranks sustain a deep drone: a rounded saw foundation and a quieter hollow pulse. Slow entry and a long low tail support held bass notes without constant pitch wobble. A strongly covered harmonic spectrum with a tidy release.

programs.name: Wide Pads 59
programs.description: Saw and pulse ranks spread left and right with a broad chorus. Their different attacks and PWM rates create width while each side retains a useful chord body. The two circuit ranks spread gently across stereo, retaining stable pitch.

programs.name: Soft Pads 60
programs.description: Pure 8' and quieter 4' sines fade in at different speeds. Pressure shapes their level, not their bypassed filters; no chorus or added hiss clouds the rounded octave. A restrained upper edge with a subtly cushioned onset.

programs.name: Amber Pads 61
programs.description: A dark saw foundation supports a later pulse glow, a broad stereo field, chorus and a faint slow ring beat. Long, unequal releases leave a warm cinematic tail after the upper color recedes. A warmer filter balance and a slightly longer body decay.

programs.name: Velvet Pads 62
programs.description: A broad saw and moving pulse cloud with deliberately stronger voice variation. Moderate drift and staggered envelopes give a haze while retaining a recognizable chord center. A covered upper register and a gently rounded release.

programs.name: Distant Pads 63
programs.description: A pure 8' sine fades in beneath a separate thin veil of filtered noise. The air arrives later and follows pressure more strongly, leaving the pitched center clean and soft. Restrained high harmonics with a longer, softer ending.

programs.name: Neon Pads 64
programs.description: A 16' foundation and an 8' upper rank form one true octave. The lighter upper voice arrives later and fades sooner, leaving a rounded low tail. A forward upper edge with a compact attack and decay.

programs.name: Hollow Pads 65
